chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Muthanna ibn Abd al-Salam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performs Hajj on behalf of another person, mentioning him in all the stations, he said: 'If he wishes, he does, and if he wishes, he does not. Allah knows that he has performed Hajj on his behalf, but he should mention him at the time of the sacrifice when he slaughters it.'
And a man does not perform Tawaf on behalf of another man while both are in Mecca, but it is permissible for him to perform Tawaf on behalf of another while the latter is absent. Narrated.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for performing Hajj and Tawaf on behalf of another person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in Hajj al-Ni'ab, emphasizing that while the agent may mention the principal at all stations, it is sufficient to do so at the time of sacrifice, as Allah’s knowledge validates the intent. It further distinguishes the rules of Tawaf, permitting it on behalf of an absent person but not when both are present, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the necessity of personal presence for certain pillars. This highlights the balance between ritual precision and the spiritual reality of divine acceptance in Shia fiqh.
